Hi Karthik,

Quick summary from our side as we start renewal conversations for our production deployment: we want to renew for 12 months and increase our reserved capacity by +40 A100-equivalent GPUs (split across us-west and us-east). The primary asks are:

- Guaranteed sustained throughput across our main inference route of >=1200 tokens/sec aggregate.
- P95 latency target at or below 180ms for our standard generation workloads (seq len ~512).
- Uptime SLA of 99.95% (we can discuss credits if missed).

Attached is a short requirements sheet (Aurora_requirements_20261005.xlsx) that lists traffic patterns and peak windows. From a procurement/contracting perspective, we also need an explicit SLA exception clause in the term amendment to cover the new guaranteed throughput levels and an initial tuning window (first 30 days) where we accept a softer p95 while kernels and routing are tuned.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these numbers, and if not, what the realistic alternative would be? We are on a tight timeline — procurement would like an agreed draft by the end of next week.

Thanks,
Lena

Karthik / team — quick feasibility notes after an ops review and a short perf sweep against Aurora-like traces:

- Capacity: +40 A100-equivalent GPUs (split 60/40 us-west/us-east) is fine from an allocation standpoint. We can provision as a dedicated reserved pool and bind Aurora’s routing to it.

- Throughput: We can reach the 1200 tok/s aggregate, but only if we enable continuous batching and increase worker concurrency and pre-warm the KV cache for hot prefixes. That increases memory pressure; we’ll need a tuned quantization profile for their model to avoid a regression.

- Latency (P95): out-of-the-box with current kernels we measured ~230ms P95 on Aurora traces. With the following mitigations we can target 200ms within 7 days and 180ms within 30 days:
  * Kernel micro-optimizations (we have 2 queued patches to reduce kernel launch overhead),
  * Prefix/KV pre-warming during peak windows,
  * Dedicated routing to avoid noisy neighbors.

- Uptime: achieving 99.95% is feasible but reduces our maintenance flexibility. Standard dedicated pools in our SLAs are 99.9%. To grant 99.95% we’d require:
  * a limited maintenance window (we propose a 1×6hr/month allowed downtime exclusion for emergency fixes),
  * a higher monthly commit (we’ll propose pricing consequent to +40 GPUs).

Proposed SLA exception (draft):
- P95 target: 180ms goal with an initial 30-day tuning period where p95 may be up to 220ms.
- Uptime: 99.95% guaranteed after the first 30 days; for the first 30 days we’ll commit to 99.9% operationally.
- Credits: 10% service credit for uptime breaches between 99.9%–99.95%, escalating to 20% for <99.9% in a billing month.

I attached a working draft of the SLA for your review (Aurora_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf). Pricing/credit percentages are placeholders — Ben please sanity-check. Marissa, we’ll need contractual wording that captures the 30-day tuning exception and the credit tiers.

-Monica

Hi Lena / Derek — thanks for the patience while we validated internally. Per Monica’s notes above, here’s the proposed path forward we are ready to offer: 

1) Capacity: Redwood to provision +40 A100-equivalent GPUs as a dedicated reserved pool (60% us-west, 40% us-east).
2) Throughput: We will tune continuous batching and pre-warm KV caches to target the 1200 tok/s aggregate.
3) Latency: Committed target: P95 = 180ms after a 30-day tuning window. We will aim for <=200ms within the first 7 days. During the first 30 days the P95 may be up to 220ms while we apply kernel and routing optimizations.
4) Uptime: Committed 99.95% after the initial 30-day ramp. For the first 30 days operationally we will target 99.9%.
5) Credits: 10% monthly service credit for uptime between 99.9%–99.95%; 20% credit for <99.9% (per billing month).

We’ve uploaded the SLA draft and the runbook to the shared links and prepared a DocuSign envelope with the term amendment and the SLA exception clause. Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/D-2026-0587 and https://docusign.com/aurora/ds-0x7a9-aurora-sla

Please confirm if you accept this approach and we’ll route the DocuSign for signature. If you want a stronger uptime guarantee faster, we can explore higher committed capacity / dedicated regional redundancy and I’ll fire off a pricing update from Ben.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line next week.

Best,
